quest.title: Kinich's Deal
quest.description: An unexpected encounter finds you just as you are planning to go to Elder Trinidad's dwelling...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Pay the Scions of the Canopy a visit

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich! Fancy meeting you here! We've actually been looking for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey there. Nice to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'll get straight to the point. I hear you accepted a proposal from Elder Trinidad?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! The, uh, Turnfire Night, you mean? Uhh... You were still his first choice, it's just... Oh geez... It's not what it looks like, promise!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Chill, it's cool. I only mention it because there's something you should know, and I suspect Elder Trinidad hasn't been completely forthcoming with you. His true intention is to resolve the Mountain King problem once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Once and for all? You mean, this'll be the last Turnfire Night ever?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That's right. He wants to use you to send the Mountain King to the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: To the Night Kingdom? You mean—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: To his death.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, whoa, whoa! Are you serious right now? You shouldn't go around blurting out accusations like that, it can get you in trouble!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Too blunt? Okay. I'll phrase it more gently...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: There is potentially a possibility that Elder Trinidad may be hoping that, during the course of the ceremony... you kill the Mountain King dead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... That's ridiculous! He told us the Mountain King is a living symbol of your tribe's glory!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: And that glory comes at a price.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: That's right. The Mountain King is a living symbol of our glory, but even this glory comes at a price.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Yes, and Nanna wasn't the first...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it because of his companion, Nanna?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Mhm. She likely won't be the last to lose her life, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still... Is killing the Mountain King really the only way? It seems so extreme...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How does he plan to kill him?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Mountain King is a unique case when it comes to Abyssal contamination. It's eaten away at him for so long that it has consumed him entirely, and the damage is irreversible.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That evil power has both driven him insane and kept him alive over the centuries. So to look at it one way, once it's completely purged from his body, the Mountain King will finally be able to rest in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: In past ceremonies, we've only purged around half of the Abyssal power. This was to strike a balance — to keep him alive, but also keep him asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Trinidad didn't say anything about how much power he wanted us to purge... But he did say there were some more details to go over before the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Then it sounds like you'll know for sure soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...If he really asks us to kill the Mountain King, what should we do?

choices.text: I think we're a little out of our depth here.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I know this must come as quite a shock, so I suggest you act like you didn't hear anything for now. But would you have time to visit the chief after your meeting with Elder Trinidad?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: I'd like to make a deal with you.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: One that comes at a very reasonable price. I'm sure you have plenty of other questions, but we can talk more later.

choices.text: Is it too late for us to back out?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Ah, mighty outlanders, you have returned. Did you have a good rest?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was, uh... pretty good, yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Glad to hear it. Things are progressing very smoothly on my end. Many of the elders have heard of your heroic deeds, including the chief. They all speak very favorably of you.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: There are still those who insist that the ceremony should be performed by the bearer of the Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo name, but they're just stuck in the past. We need to move with the times.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Plus, Kinich doesn't wanna do it anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Exactly. So now, it's time for us to discuss the finer details of the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: We covered the fire-lighting part of the proceedings yesterday. The next part is the purification of the Mountain King.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How does that work?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: It's quite simple — you just need to use the sacred flame. We've done it plenty of times before and it's always very routine. I'm sure you won't have any problems.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: One point I'd like to stress, though, is that you need to burn away as much of the Abyssal energy as you possibly can. The more we dispel, the longer the Mountain King will remain asleep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Asleep," huh...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Precisely. In previous years, the flame bearer has often been unable to dispel a sufficient amount of Abyssal energy. That's the only reason why we have to perform the ceremony on a regular basis.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: But I understand that you have a lot of experience fighting against the Abyss. And you seemed to wield the sacred flame quite effortlessly yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: With your help, I'm optimistic that this time we can dispel all the remaining Abyssal energy from the Mountain King's body, freeing us from this ever-looming threat for many years to come.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it. Anything else we need to know?

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: So this doesn't faze you at all, huh? You clearly have a lot of confidence in yourself, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: That's all you really need to know. The ceremony is in three days. I'll come and fetch you when we're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: In the meantime, feel free to take a look around our settlement. It would mean a lot to the elders if you got to know some of our people.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: And if you wouldn't mind helping them out with a few errands here and there, that would be even better.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So now we have extra errands to run? Maybe we should add a little extra to the price...

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: Haha, just a humble suggestion, that's all. It will help you gain the respect of our people, and as a mighty hero, I truly believe that's what you deserve.

dialogues.speaker: Trinidad
dialogues.text: I'll be sticking around over the next few days, so if you have any questions, you know where to find me.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich! Elder Trinidad said that—

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I can tell. It's written on your faces.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: #Is that {NICKNAME} and Paimon? Forgive me for not being there to welcome you on your arrival. That should have been my duty as chief.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, Chief Wayna.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: I only heard the news from Trinidad yesterday, so I asked Kinich to invite you over for a quick chat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's our pleasure.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Hehe... I believe Kinich has already filled you in, so I'll get straight to the point. Firstly, I fully endorse your appointment as flame bearers for the upcoming Turnfire Night.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: However, I would like to request that you take steps to ensure the Mountain King's safety.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Every child of our tribe grows up hearing the tales of our heroes, from Yupanqui the Fire-Bringer, to Burkina and the Mountain King who fought against the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: This is our history and our heritage, the source of our pride and the center of our faith.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: To kill the Mountain King would be to destroy our spirit... I would never be able to face our ancestors in the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Nanna's death was a great tragedy, and I do not blame Trinidad for the actions he has taken. Nevertheless, I cannot allow any harm to come to the Mountain King. The very roots of our identity are at stake.

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: My honored guests, please give this matter your serious consideration.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there no solution that would satisfy both sides?

dialogues.speaker: Wayna
dialogues.text: Perhaps there is. But despite all our attempts to contain the situation over the years, we have not found it. Right now, I should like to hear where you stand on this matter.

choices.text: I'm inclined to honor your request.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: Though I sense that your mind is not yet made up, I am still comforted by your words. There are three days left before the ceremony. I hope they will bring you clarity.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So Kinich, earlier, you were saying that—

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Let's walk and talk. I'll show you around the tribe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That works too. Paimon needs to get some air after this...

choices.text: I'm inclined to honor my agreement with Trinidad.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: I must say, I find this troubling, though I'm sure you need more time to consider it fully. No matter, there are still three days left before the ceremony. I hope they will bring you clarity.

choices.text: I need some time to mull this over.

response.speaker: Wayna
response.text: I understand. There are still three days left before the ceremony. I hope they will bring you clarity.

choices.text: Paimon, let's sneak off to some other tribe tonight...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Running away won't solve anything... You just need some time to think this through, that's all. Don't worry, we'll come up with something if we put our heads together!

response.speaker: Chief
response.text: Thank you both. There are still three days left before the ceremony. I hope they will bring you clarity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich, Paimon finally understands why you turned Trinidad down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You knew what he was planning, didn't you? That's why you didn't wanna be the flame bearer this time, 'cause it's a double-edged sword. The whole Mora thing was just a sneaky excuse!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Double-edged sword is right. But my response wasn't merely an excuse: To solve this exceptional problem, an exceptional price must be paid.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you saying you have a plan?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm working on it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Well c'mon then, let's hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: In a moment. Didn't you have a question you were about to ask me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... What was it again? ...Oh! Right! We need to talk about Ajaw, he's completely unhinged!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a point... where is he today?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I agree that he has a problem. He needs disciplining, so I hired him a teacher.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got him a teacher? Oh, Paimon would love to see him get scolded for bad behavior!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, moving on — when we ran into Ajaw, he said you two were investigating some Abyss thing together... Is that related to the whole Mountain King situation?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yes. That's the angle I've been working on.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm a Saurian hunter, but I occasionally hunt the Abyss, too. One time, I was pursuing some purple demonic dogs when I accidentally entered a hidden space.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I did some research after the fact. Apparently, they're known as "Beastly Rifts," and there are many of them of all different sizes. That's where those purple dogs were coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: So, if we can locate one of these Beastly Rifts, clear the monsters out, and move the Mountain King inside... he'd be able to continue living, but without posing a threat to the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! That sounds kind of crazy... Would it really work?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: It's not without its risks, of course. There's a lot of unknowns in the equation. For instance, for all we know, a prolonged period inside the rift could make the Mountain King's condition worse.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Still, we desperately need something like this — even just as a temporary measure. You've seen the conflict the issue is causing in our tribe for yourselves, and believe me, it's been a long time coming.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The chief is adamant about keeping the Mountain King alive, whatever happens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can understand... It's less about the Mountain King, and more about preserving your culture and heritage.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Yes, but on the flip side, you've got people like Elder Trinidad, who is more concerned about protecting the people he cares about, now and into the future.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: And he has every right to take that view. It's one thing to try and preserve the last remnants of a glorious past, but making your kin pay the price for it?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: No one can seriously tell them that's a fair trade.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right, there's no easy answers here... Let's leave that to one side for a moment and assume we go with your plan. How do you actually intend to find one of these Beastly Rifts?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cause at least in our experience, the dogs open the rifts when they wanna attack us, not the other way around.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I think I know a way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you really gonna do this?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: You have any better ideas?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not at the moment, but... It just feels like using the power of the Abyss for our own ends isn't gonna end well...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: After all, the Abyss is what turned the Mountain King into a monster in the first place. People are gonna think you've lost your marbles...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If it doesn't end well, then that's the price we pay. Everything in the world comes at a price... Even when Yupanqui the Fire-Bringer stole the Turnfire, it cost him dearly.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The Mountain King's erratic outbursts have brought tensions within the tribe to a boiling point. Unless this gets resolved quickly, everyone will be stuck in a stalemate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... So what's this "deal" you wanted to make with us? We're hardly experts on exploiting Abyssal power...

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: All I need you to do is keep people away from me.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm getting harassed on a daily basis by people trying to convince me to be the flame bearer. I can't afford to waste all my energy dealing with them.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: If you help me out, there'll be a gift for you in return.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, what kind of gift?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Something well worth your while, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, but how do we keep people away?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Just keep doing what you've been doing — ingratiate yourself with the tribespeople, so everyone comes to terms with the fact that we have a new flame bearer.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: That way, I won't have an endless stream of people coming to beg me to join the ceremony, and I can focus on finding a way to summon the Beastly Rift.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Then, when the day of the ceremony comes, we'll move the Mountain King into his new home.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still sounds pretty crazy... Even for a daredevil like you, that's dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And even if it works — what if neither Chief Wayna nor Elder Trinidad are happy with it? Have you thought about what you'd do then?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: At least the two of them would finally be on the same side of the issue, leaving only me on the opposing side.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The tribe needs leaders like them far more than a Saurian hunter for hire like me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Either way, sounds like there's no mora in this for you.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hah. Can I take that to mean we have a deal?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For sure. And who knows, maybe we'll come up with an even better solution to all of this in the next couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Great. Well, for the next couple of days, please spend some time among the tribe and lend a hand wherever you can. I'm sure everyone will be swept off their feet when they meet our new flame bearer.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Good luck to us both.
